knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)

<!-- #region -->
### Version Problems

In order to follow the examples in this documentation site, you should have the latest version of `plotly.core` installed (`r version`), as detailed in the [Getting Started](getting-started.html) guide. These pages are written for `plotly.core`, which is a different package from the legacy `plotly` R package: code written for `plotly` (`plot_ly()`, `layout()`, `subplot()`, ...) will not work here, and vice versa. `plotly.core` bundles its own copy of the Plotly.js rendering engine, so figures look the same wherever they are rendered. Read on for details about troubleshooting `plotly.core` in other environments such as Dash.

### Import Problems

Most loading problems can be traced back to having multiple or outdated versions of `plotly.core` installed. It's often worthwhile to uninstall before following the [Getting Started](getting-started.html) instructions from scratch. You can run the following commands in the console to fully remove `plotly.core` before installing again:

```
remove.packages('plotly.core')
```

> Problems can also arise if you have a file named `plotly.core.R` in the same directory as the code you are executing.

### Dash Problems

If you are encountering problems using `plotly.core` with [Dash](https://dashr.plotly.com/) please first ensure that you have upgraded `dash` to the latest version, which will automatically upgrade `dash-core-components` to the latest version, ensuring that Dash is using an up-to-date version of the Plotly.js rendering engine. If this does not resolve your issue, please visit our [Dash Community Forum](https://community.plotly.com/) and we will be glad to help you out.

This is an example of a `plotly.core` graph inside `dash`:
<!-- #endregion -->

```{r eval=FALSE}
library(plotly.core)

fig <- go_figure() |>
  add_bar(x = c(0, 1, 2), y = c(3, 7, 9))
#fig

library(dash)
library(dashCoreComponents)
library(dashHtmlComponents)

app <- Dash$new()

app$layout(
  htmlDiv(
    list(
      dccGraph(
        id = "graph",
        figure = fig
      )
    )
  )
)

#app$run_server()
```

Use `app$run_server()` to run the dash app.

### Static Image Export Problems

`plotly.core` does not use the `orca` executable. `save_image()` exports figures with headless Chrome (driven by the chromote package). If export fails because no browser is found, set the `CHROMOTE_CHROME` environment variable to the complete path of a Chrome or Chromium-based browser, or download Chrome Headless Shell once with `chromote::chrome_versions_add("latest-stable", "chrome-headless-shell")`. See [Static Image Export](static-image-export.html) for details.
